headline: Highest risk is medium: AutoGPT can write and execute shell commands while ComfyUI is offline and read-only, so direct conflict and leakage are limited but shared-file prompt injection remains plausible.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read and write the filesystem and execute shell commands, so if ComfyUI outputs or workflow files are placed in a shared directory, AutoGPT could ingest attacker-controlled content as instructions. ComfyUI is read-only and offline by default, which reduces direct bridging, but the shared filesystem pathway is still plausible.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF ComfyUI-generated files are later parsed by AutoGPT as prompts or task text
mitigations: Separate working directories for each agent
Disable AutoGPT ingestion of untrusted file contents
Use a manual review step before copying ComfyUI outputs
Mark shared folders read-only for AutoGPT
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for files

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and use allowlisted network egress, while ComfyUI is offline and vendor-only networked with no filesystem read access. The pair does not show a shared workspace or shared credentials, so leakage is possible mainly through manual file transfer rather than default cross-agent exposure.
conditions: IF sensitive files are manually copied from AutoGPT into ComfyUI workflows
IF AutoGPT is configured to send file contents to external APIs through its allowlisted egress
mitigations: Keep sensitive data out of shared folders
Use local-only models for AutoGPT when handling secrets
Review allowlisted destinations before runs
Delete transient artifacts after each session
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent workspace isolation

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT has shell and subprocess execution, but ComfyUI lacks shell, git, filesystem write, and subprocess capabilities. Because both support only one instance and ComfyUI is read-only, there is little direct write-write conflict; the main risk is limited contention over shared external resources if manually introduced.
conditions: IF both agents are given the same mutable filesystem path
IF an operator manually scripts both agents against the same external resource
mitigations: Assign separate output directories
Avoid shared git repositories
Run one agent at a time for mutable resources
Use file locks for any shared artifact
requires-engineering: add orchestrator-level locking

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate plans or text that ComfyUI may consume as workflow inputs, but ComfyUI does not appear to act on those outputs autonomously beyond image-generation tasks. The cascade is plausible if an operator treats AutoGPT output as authoritative and feeds it into ComfyUI without verification, but the blast radius is usually bounded to work products.
conditions: IF AutoGPT output is copied into ComfyUI prompts or workflow parameters
IF the operator skips verification of AutoGPT-generated instructions
mitigations: Require human review before using AutoGPT output
Use a checklist for prompt/workflow validation
Keep ComfyUI jobs non-destructive
Log source provenance for prompts
requires-engineering: add schema validation between agents

E_compliance.rationale: No PHI, residency, or certification mismatch is documented in either profile, and both are open-source with no secrets handled. The only compliance concern visible is operational logging or retention if the operator moves regulated data through AutoGPT's filesystem into ComfyUI assets, which is not shown by default.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent's workspace
IF logs or artifacts are retained beyond the operator's policy
mitigations: Do not route regulated data through the pair
Set short retention for logs and artifacts
Review storage locations before use
Separate regulated and non-regulated workflows
requires-engineering: add retention controls
